title: Dostarlimab (Jemperli) alone
context_label: Previously treated dMMR or MSI-high endometrial cancer
schedule_label: Every 3 weeks × 4. Dose 5 three weeks later, then every 6 weeks.
schedule_summary: One infusion every three weeks for four doses. Dose 5 is three weeks after dose 4. After dose 5 the interval is six weeks, while treatment remains suitable.
purpose: The aim is to help your immune system recognise and control the cancer.
indication_text: This immunotherapy is for advanced or recurrent womb cancer that progressed during or after platinum treatment and has a tumour test showing mismatch repair deficiency or high microsatellite instability.
administration_text: Dostarlimab goes into a vein over about 30 minutes. Only dostarlimab is used on this pathway. Keep the immunotherapy alert card with you after treatment too.
monitoring_summary: Report extreme tiredness, dizziness or unusual thirst between visits.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Dostarlimab
agents.explanation: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.mechanism: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new cough, diarrhoea, severe fatigue or rash even after the final dose.

questions.a: Talk through this with your nurse and write the answer on your appointment sheet.

support.title: Immune alert card
support.text: Show the card to any clinician treating you, even months after your last infusion. Include the date of your last dose.

support.title: Between infusions
support.text: Routine sickness risk is minimal. Report new diarrhoea or vomiting to oncology before treating it yourself because it can reflect immune inflammation.

teachback: When is dose 5 due, and which symptoms would you report even after your last dose?
consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Call urgently for new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, severe weakness or a blistering rash.

evidence.title: GARNET
evidence.interpretation: In the GARNET trial, measurable tumour shrinkage was seen in about 46 in 100 evaluable people in the mismatch repair deficient or MSI-high endometrial cancer group.
evidence.limitations: This was a single-arm trial. A response rate does not tell us how long someone will live or how the medicine compares directly with another treatment.
